ticket.title: Detect agent thrash and dead ends from telemetry, alert on the SSE stream
acceptance_criteria:
SCOPE 2026-11-07, from plans/GB-243.md section 12.3. Third runtime consumer, and the one with the most room to be wrong.

WHAT: detect two shapes of stuck agent from the span stream.
  Gate thrash: 3 or more consecutive `outfeed gate` failures on the same step, same (task_key, worktree).
  Search thrash: 5 or more consecutive read/MCP calls within 60 seconds with no file edit, plan update or gate run between them.
Surface a `ThrashAlert` over the benchwork SSE stream, and optionally a recovery hint in gaugeblock-mcp responses.

WHY THE SECOND SHAPE EXISTS: a gate failure is at least a signal that something was attempted. An agent reading file after file for a minute and changing nothing is the failure mode with no crash and no error - it looks like work in the span log and costs tokens, and it is invisible to every other instrument in the suite.

WHAT MAKES THIS HARD, and must be decided before code:
  Detection needs state across spans, so it cannot be computed by a stateless query over the log; something holds a window per (session_id, task_key). Where that state lives decides whether the alert survives a daemon restart, and whether two benchwork instances double-count.
  "Consecutive" needs a definition that survives interleaving. Two agents on one task interleave their spans, and a naive last-N list will read one agent's read calls as another's thrash.
  An edit is not the only thing that un-sticks an agent: a plan update, a gate run, a commit, an explicit defer. The un-stick set is a list and it needs writing down.
  False positives are expensive here - an alert on normal exploration trains the operator to ignore alerts, which is the same failure as a noisy Law 12 warning.

SEQUENCING: this depends on spans existing for CLI and MCP calls (GB-297 and GB-298), because today only sawhorse emits any. Building the detector first would mean tuning thresholds against a stream that carries one producer.

Done when: both shapes are detected against synthetic span sequences with an interleaved two-agent case in the tests, the un-stick set is documented and tested, a restarted daemon does not re-alert on the same window, and the alert carries enough context (task, step, count, window) to act on without reading the log.
